title: Multiply and Sum Correlator
description: A sample-by-sample correlation walkthrough with two aligned waveforms, per-sample product arithmetic, and a zero-centered running-total bar.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Correlation
Signals and Systems

learningObjectives: Calculate a correlation sum sample by sample
Demonstrate why matching frequencies accumulate and mismatched ones cancel
Relate bin spacing to exact orthogonality
prerequisites: A signal is an array of samples

equations: sum = sum over n of x[n] * t[n]
assumptions: Both signals are unit-amplitude sines starting at zero phase
limitations: Real correlation must also test the quadrature component to be phase-independent; that is handled by the in-phase/quadrature sim

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through calculation with visible intermediate arithmetic
keyQuestions: Why is every product non-negative when the frequencies match?
What does the running total do when they do not match?
commonMisconceptions: That correlation is a complicated operation rather than multiply-and-add
That a mismatched frequency gives a small positive value rather than cancellation
assessmentOpportunities: Sketch the running total for a one-bin-offset test frequency
